clue.text: Mostly need warm hat in a storm, he might say

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so these letters are tossed into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word need is kept

explanation.surface: A forecaster warns that you will need a warm hat in the coming storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims NEED to NEE; with WARMHAT that gives ten letters, which 'in a storm' rearranges. The definition leans on the surface: a forecaster is the one who would say this.
explanation.definitionFit: A television forecaster is the sort of person who would predict a storm and advise headgear.

clue.text: Extra passengers fit in this carriage

indicators.note: the letters that fit inside the run of words extra passengers are taken out

explanation.surface: A carriage roomy enough to squeeze in additional riders.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle is called by this name.

clue.text: Conspirator hiding regularly among rowan trees

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of rowan trees is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A plotter hides out in a grove of mountain ash.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates invented the Popish Plot of 1678.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates fabricated the Popish Plot, making him history's famous conspirator by that name.

clue.text: Soldiers taken, disheartened, into battle for several days

indicators.note: into means the soldiers and the trimmed word go inside the word for battle

parts.note: a battle is a fight
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the middle letters, of the word taken is removed

explanation.surface: Troops are captured and dispirited during a fight lasting days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips AKE from TAKEN to leave TN.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of fourteen days is a fair reading of several days.

clue.text: Part of leg most painful in a cold part of north London?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: in means the superlative for most painful sits inside the other letters

parts.note: Hendon is a district of north London
illest means most sick or most painful

explanation.surface: A leg injury feels worst on a chilly day in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Hendon is a suburb of north London; 'in' puts the superlative just after its first letter, so the leg part is hidden in a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: The tendon joining calf muscle to heel bone is an anatomical part of the leg.

clue.text: Behind goal after boring header's disallowed

indicators.note: after places the goal word behind the trimmed word
the header, the first letter, of the word for boring is not allowed

parts.note: drear means dull or boring
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A football report: a goal comes after a dull header is ruled out.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'header' a ball nodded in; here it is the first letter of DREAR, dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The back part of something, or one's bottom, is called the behind.

clue.text: Daft-sounding fool used to make chips

indicators.note: sounding means the words are heard said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: daft means silly
to con is to fool or trick

explanation.surface: A fool who sounds stupid is put to work frying potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' works on 'Daft' alone: SILLY heard becomes SILI. 'Chips' looks like fried potatoes; it means microchips.
explanation.definitionFit: Microchips are made from wafers of this semiconductor element.

clue.text: Hurtful piece from newspaper

definitions.meaning: a ... remark is wounding or hurtful
a press ... is an article clipped out of a paper

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both wounding and a clipped press article, matching the two halves.

clue.text: Fancy US investigators wearing suit

indicators.note: wearing means the suit word goes around the investigators like clothing

parts.note: to suit is to fit
G-men are FBI agents in the USA

explanation.surface: FBI agents decked out in a fancy suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is something imagined, like a product of the imagination.

clue.text: Troubles among ladies and gents?

parts.note: among means in
conveniences is a British euphemism for public toilets, labelled Ladies and Gents

explanation.surface: Problems arising in public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the public toilets are often signed Ladies and Gents and called conveniences.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles, as a verb, means bothers or puts out, a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Miss fighting aboard eg retreating schooners?

indicators.note: aboard means the girl and the fight go inside, as on board a ship
retreating means the letters of eg are read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a miss, a girl
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A girl at war on board ships in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns EG round to GE, and 'aboard' puts the girl and the fighting inside it. A schooner is a sailing ship, but also a tall sherry or beer glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooners are large drinking glasses, examples of drinking vessels; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Coal left in appropriate container

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the container

parts.note: a sack is the natural bag to hold coal

explanation.surface: Coal left in a suitable bag.
explanation.definitionFit: This is small or powdered coal, coal dust mixed with fragments.

clue.text: Maybe churchwarden's religious lesson in school

parts.note: pi is an informal word for pious or religious
PE, physical education, is a school lesson

explanation.surface: A churchwarden gives religious teaching at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a long clay smoking pipe as well as a parish officer; ''s' is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe, so this is an example.

clue.text: Match over between Britain and Denmark: one could get bitter here

indicators.note: between means the reversed word goes between the two letters for Britain
over means the word for match is turned back to front

parts.note: to agree is to match
DEN is a short form for Denmark

explanation.surface: A match is over between Britain and Denmark, and the loser is bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the match word back to front, giving EERGA, set between B and R. Bitter is a British style of beer, not resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor area of a pub is where you might be served a pint of bitter ale.

clue.text: Maybe deal drugs principally behind court

indicators.note: behind puts the drug letter after the courting word

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: principally means the first letter of the word drugs

explanation.surface: A dealer peddling drugs behind a courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a kind of softwood, so 'Maybe' flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is fir or pine timber, an example of this material.

clue.text: Argonaut's wit?

parts.note: an Argonaut was a Greek sailor, so his humour is that of a Greek seaman, and 'salt' is a sailor

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means refined, elegant wit, from Attica (Athens); a salt is also a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes refined, delicate humour of the kind associated with ancient Athens.

clue.text: I whistle Stones medley one hates hearing?

indicators.note: a medley mixes tunes together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone loathes listening to me whistling Rolling Stones songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like listening; it is a court hearing, where an unhelpful witness is hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, a witness who turns against the side that called them is treated as one hostile.

clue.text: Servicemen took flight offered as prize in draw

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are servicemen
fled means ran away, took flight

explanation.surface: Airmen escaped and were given away as a lottery prize.
explanation.definitionFit: An item put up in a lottery as a prize has been disposed of this way.

clue.text: Checks what's included in fare before holidays

indicators.note: before places the inner letters ahead of the holiday word
what is included in a word is its inside, the letters without the ends

parts.note: rests are breaks or holidays

explanation.surface: Checking what the fare covers ahead of the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to halt or stop it, a synonym in its verb sense.

clue.text: Scrap material? Journalist was fuming

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter was furious about a scrap of material.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fuming is to be furious, so it matches being in a violent temper.

clue.text: With peanut assortment, don't supply squash

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Avoid giving a squash drink with a bag of mixed nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as an adjective, as in pliant: it reinforces 'assortment' by saying the letters bend into a new shape. 'squash' is a verb, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash a rebellion is to quash or stop it entirely, a verb phrase sense.

clue.text: During TV broadcast fellow's upset top thinkers

parts.note: during means in

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard said, not written

parts.note: telly is informal British for TV
gent's, a fellow's, gives these letters

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for top is turned upside down

parts.note: A1 means first-class or top, written as AI

explanation.surface: A man gets upset during a TV broadcast about leading intellectuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns TELLY into the sound TELLI; 'upset' turns AI into IA. A1 means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The educated intellectual elite of a society are its thinkers.

clue.text: In competition, vehicle overturns: champion breaking down

indicators.note: In means the vehicle and champion go inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a competition

indicators.note: overturns means the vehicle word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a king is a champion, the best

explanation.surface: In a race, a car flips and the champion is overcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone breaking down emotionally under strain is said to be losing control in this way.

clue.text: Democrat leader once able to shake off Republican, then win

indicators.note: to shake off means the Republican letter is removed

parts.note: clever means able
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A Democrat able to shake off a Republican rival and triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was a Democratic US president, serving two non-consecutive terms.

clue.text: European in work unit picked up explosive

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the letters are lifted, read bottom to top
in means the European goes inside the work unit

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
a Dane is a European

explanation.surface: A European in a work team is caught with a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: EDANERG, read upwards by 'picked up', gives the answer. 'picked up' looks like a homophone but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb is a small explosive device.

clue.text: Endlessly search back street in Paris for hairdresser

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for search is removed

parts.note: to frisk is to search a person

indicators.note: back means the French word for street is reversed

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Searching the backstreets of Paris for a hairdresser.
explanation.definitionFit: This is French for a hairdresser, also used in English.

clue.text: Munch cold meat with pickle for starters

parts.note: ham is a meat

indicators.note: for starters means the first letter of pickle

explanation.surface: Eat cold ham with pickle as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew noisily, a synonym for munch.

clue.text: Film son with family

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A movie about a son and his relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin film or layer on a surface, like on hot milk, is a synonym.
